title: Nonviral delivery of chemically modified tRNA rescues nonsense mutations in cystic fibrosis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the three GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series linked to this PubMed ID and downloaded two processed tables: GSE326898 ribosome-profiling counts (78,686 Ensembl gene rows x 9 samples, 0.78 MB gzipped) and GSE326462 tRNA-seq counts (277 transfer-RNA gene rows x 27 samples, 21 KB). GSE303837 adds 9 RNA-seq samples plus differential-expression CSVs. I also probed the Science supplementary-material and article URLs with the shared fetch helper: all returned HTTP 403 (blocked/paywalled), and Europe PMC reports no PubMed Central ID, no open access and no supplementary files for this paper.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the thing that would make an ML project here: that >1000 ionizable lipids were screened, that N1-methyladenosine at tRNA position 57/58 raised premature-stop-codon readthrough up to 10.6-fold, and all organoid/mouse efficacy numbers. These come from the abstract and press summaries (NIH Research Matters, C&EN), not from any file I opened. I never saw a lipid structure, a SMILES string or a delivery readout.

a1_downloadable.note: The only ML-relevant dataset — the >1000-ionizable-lipid screen with its delivery readouts — exists only in the Science supplementary materials, which return HTTP 403 and are not in PubMed Central (no PMCID, Europe PMC flags isOpenAccess=N, hasSuppl=N). No Zenodo/Dryad/figshare deposit found on the DOI and no preprint with an open supplement. The GEO sequencing series do download freely, but they are not the lipid data.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: For the lipid project the label (lung delivery efficiency per lipid) is unseen and unobtainable. For the GEO data, any readthrough label would have to be constructed from ribosome-profiling coverage past stop codons, but the deposited Ribo-seq file is gene-level counts only (78,686 genes x 9 samples), with no codon-resolution profiles — so the label would have to be built from raw reads we are not allowed to download.

a3_inputs_present.note: No lipid structures (SMILES or any machine-readable chemistry) are accessible; lipid identities are internal codes like TTP-3 named only in the text.

a4_units_stated.note: What I did open is unambiguous: integer read counts per gene or per tRNA gene, with sample names in the header. Units for the inaccessible lipid screen are unknown.

a5_enough_rows.note: The experimental unit in all downloadable data is the sequencing sample: 9 (Ribo-seq) + 27 (tRNA-seq time course) + 9 (RNA-seq) = 45 samples across three series, all from human bronchial epithelial cell lines. Gene rows are features, not independent examples. Far below the ~1,500-row bar; even the claimed lipid screen (>1000 lipids, unverified) would be borderline for regression.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Everything downloadable fits trivially in memory; this is the one check that passes comfortably and it does not rescue the candidate.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: GEO sample counts (9/27/9) match the series metadata; I cannot cross-check against the paper because the full text is paywalled. The >1000-lipid figure could not be checked against any file.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable for the lipid screen because no label file is reachable. For the GEO data the measurements are genuine (sequencing read counts), but no therapeutic-outcome label exists in them at all.

existing_models.name: AGILE (AI-Guided Ionizable Lipid Engineering), Nature Communications 2024
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified — I retrieved the title and abstract listing only, not the paper's evaluation details.

existing_models.name: TransMA, a multimodal deep-learning model for ionizable lipid nanoparticle transfection, Briefings in Bioinformatics 2025
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified — abstract listing only; described as combining a 3D-structure transformer with a 1D molecular model.

existing_models.name: LightGBM lipid-nanoparticle predictor (Acta Pharmaceutica Sinica B 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: Search snippet reports R-squared above 0.87, split not stated; I did not open the paper to confirm.

existing_models.name: Extended stop-codon-context readthrough predictor (Nature Communications 2024) and genome-scale drug-induced readthrough models (Nature Genetics 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified; both report predicting premature-stop-codon readthrough from local sequence context, including for CFTR nonsense alleles.

backbone.name: ChemBERTa or MolFormer (molecular language models) would fit the lipid-structure task; none fits 45 bulk sequencing samples
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice if the data existed
backbone.licence: Backbone licences are permissive; irrelevant because the data is inaccessible

integration.partner_dataset: LipidDB / published ionizable-lipid transfection datasets, joinable on InChIKey — but only if this paper's lipid structures were released, which they are not.
integration.join_key: InChIKey (not present in any accessible file)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do lipids selected for messenger-RNA delivery also deliver transfer RNA, or does cargo type change the structure-activity rules? — a good question that this paper's inaccessible supplement would answer and the public GEO files cannot.

controls.positive_control: The GEO series do contain untreated, negative-control and wild-type-CFTR arms, so a differential-expression sanity check is possible — but that is statistics, not a model.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is meaningless at n=45 samples.
controls.external_validation: None available for any task definable from the accessible files.

honest_claim_h3: Nothing publicly downloadable from this paper supports a predictive claim; the only honest statement is that 45 bulk sequencing samples show transcriptome and tRNA-abundance changes after suppressor-tRNA treatment in one cell-line background.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the chemical structure of a fat-like delivery molecule to predict how well it carries therapeutic RNA into lung cells.
plain_idea.train_on: Intended input: each of the >1000 ionizable lipids screened in this paper, as a chemical structure, plus the nanoparticle recipe. Verified example count: unknown, because the screen's data was never accessible to me.
plain_idea.predict: Intended output: delivery efficiency of suppressor transfer RNA to lung tissue, measured in the paper by reporter readthrough or protein restoration assays. I could not see which assay or what scale.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups formulating inhaled RNA drugs choose which lipids to synthesise next, and a cargo-specific model would redirect that choice; here, though, the information needed to build it is locked in a paywalled supplement.

more_or_better_data.why: The accessible data is 45 bulk sequencing samples; the lipid screen that might have been bigger or cargo-specific than existing training sets is unavailable, so there is no data to compare.

confidence_score.why: With three replicates per condition and no accessible per-lipid replicate measurements, there is no basis for calibrated per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: Existing ionizable-lipid predictors are recent (2022-2025) and include multimodal deep models (TransMA, AGILE); without this paper's screen we would have no new data with which to challenge them.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The first condition fails outright: we cannot obtain the paper's feature/label table at all, so no baseline comparison on a shared split is constructible.

ml_idea: The attractive project was: predict suppressor-transfer-RNA lung delivery efficiency from ionizable-lipid chemical structure (a molecular language model such as ChemBERTa, frozen, with a small regression head), and test whether lipids optimised for messenger RNA transfer to transfer-RNA cargo. A secondary idea — predict stop-codon readthrough from sequence context using the ribosome-profiling data — fails because the deposited Ribo-seq file is gene-level counts, not codon-resolution coverage.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from the files I actually downloaded (0.78 MB and 21 KB gzipped, ~40 MB uncompressed); no timing needed because no modelling task survives.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Try to fetch the Science supplementary materials — one HTTP request. It returns 403, there is no PubMed Central copy, and no repository deposit, which kills the lipid project in under a minute.

verdict_reason: The only ML-worthy asset (>1000-lipid delivery screen) is behind the Science paywall and returns HTTP 403 with no PubMed Central or repository copy (A1, A3 fail); the freely downloadable data is 45 bulk sequencing samples of gene-level counts with no outcome label and no codon-resolution readthrough measurements (A2, A5, A8 fail).
